item.title: RPI football beats Ithaca, earns 1st berth in NCAA playoffs since 2021
item.description: RPI quarterback Justin McCormcak jumps through a hole during a game against Hobart on Sept. 26 in Troy. (Jim Franco/Times Union) Senior tight end Grayson Hunter caught two touchdown passes as the RPI football team edged host Ithaca 14-10 on Saturday to earn the program's first trip to the NCAA Division III playoffs since 2021. The Engineers (7-2 overall, 6-0 Liberty League) won their sixth straight game to secure at least a share of the title with Ithaca (7-2, 6-1). RPI gets the Liberty League's automatic bid to the NCAAs because of the head-to-head tiebreaker. "It's huge," RPI coach Ralph Isernia said. "It's something we've been working for, especially with this senior group the last four years. The time in the weight room and the time on the practice field, time in film meetings, all that stuff." RPI, which snapped a four-game losing streak against Ithaca, can win the league outright by beating Union College for the Dutchman Shoes Trophy in Troy next Saturday. Hunter, a backup behind starter Josh Young, made a diving 15-yard touchdown catch from starting quarterback Micah Balzarini for a 7-7 tie with 1:16 left in the second quarter. With 4:22 left in the third quarter, Hunter caught a 19-yard pass from backup quarterback Justin McCormack on a ball that was tipped by an Ithaca defender to put RPI ahead 14-10. "Certainly, there's a lot of attention that goes to Josh Young, and that's understandable," Isernia said. "But (Hunter) is able to get open and he's made plays for us this entire year." Isernia said McCormack came into the game for Balzarini by design. "Obviously, he brings another dimension with the run game and he's also an extremely effective passer as well," Isernia said. RPI's defense held Ithaca well below its league-leading average of 40.3 points per game. Defensive linemen Owen Boland and Cameron Keeperman combined on a sack of quarterback Michael Reed that helped stop a late Bombers drive. On the game's final play, Ithaca threw a Hail Mary pass from the RPI 48 that fell incomplete in a crowd in the end zone. RPI's Aidan Bekkenhuis was credited with the breakup. item.title: Messi's Miami cling to second spot on dramatic final MLS day
item.description: Lionel Messi's Inter Miami are guaranteed homefield advantage in at least their opening two rounds of post-season (Megan Briggs) Lionel Messi's Inter Miami clung on for second place in the Eastern Conference with a wasteful 3-3 draw against Charlotte on the final day of the MLS regular season Saturday. The Argentine superstar set up the first two goals at Miami's Nu Stadium, both from corners, to procure the reigning champions home-field advantage in at least their opening two rounds of the playoffs. Ian Fray, Luis Suarez and Rodrigo De Paul racked up three first-half strikes for Inter Miami before Liel Abada's brace soon after the break sparked a comeback sealed by Rodolfo Aloko's late strike in a game characterized by awful defending at both ends. A single point proved enough. Miami finished the regular season second on 60, as third-place New England Revolution failed to take advantage with a surprise 1-0 loss at Orlando, finishing on 58. Messi's men will now face the Columbus Crew to begin the playoffs. Runaway leaders Nashville broke the all-time MLS points record with a whopping 77 after beating Cincinnati 2-0. Though he did not get on the scoresheet himself Saturday, Messi's 26 goals this season are still almost certain to seal his second straight golden boot award. Petar Musa, whose FC Dallas were in action later Saturday, would need to score five to prevent Messi becoming the first player to win back-to-back MLS Golden Boots. Charlotte had an early goal ruled out in the Miami clash for handball against Idan Toklomati, who set up Abada after intercepting Casemiro's weak defensive header back to the goalkeeper. In the 14th minute, Messi's corner fell unexpectedly to Charlotte's Luca de la Torre, who spooned it up for Fray to open the scoring for Miami. Another Messi corner in the 33rd minute found Suarez wide open at the near post. The Uruguayan glanced in his header for 2-0, with Messi picking up the assist. De Paul made it three before halftime, given time and space by Charlotte's defense to slam a long-range shot low to the goalkeeper's right and into the side netting. Early in the second half Abada pulled back a goal for the visitors, blasting home substitute Tyger Smalls' sharp cut-back pass from Ashley Westwood's incisive aerial through ball. Minutes later, Messi uncharacteristically steered wide a straightforward header from the edge of the six-yard box. In the 90th minute, Aloko bagged the equalizer, responding first to the ball as Smalls' shot ricocheted off the post. item.description: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - NOVEMBER 07: Austin Bashi reacts after a victory against Carlos Calderon in a featherweight fight during the UFC Fight Night event at Meta APEX on November 07, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Zuffa LLC) Austin Bashi returned to the featherweight win column earlier tonight (Sat., Nov. 7, 2026) at UFC Vegas 124 LIVE on Paramount+ from inside Meta Apex in Las Vegas, Nevada, stopping Octagon newcomer Carlos Calderon with a dominant first-round submission (rear-naked choke). Bashi, who lost his last UFC appearance to Jose Delgado, came into Saturday’s contest a massive betting favorite. That’s because Bashi is considered on the best rising prospects at 145 pounds and the fact that Calderon was stepping up on just a few days notice. It was a tough ask for Calderon and a prime opportunity for Bashi to outshine a UFC newbie. Calderon, who came over from Fury FC, didn’t have any trouble firing out the gate and trying to make it a brawl. Unfortunately for him, Bashi didn’t need long to bring this fight to the ground. Once there, the 25-year-old was able to work his way to Calderon’s back and locked in the rear-naked choke. Calderon fought for a few moments before tapping and putting an end to his UFC debut. This week’s initial CFP rankings added even more emphasis to this week’s result at Notre Dame Stadium after Freeman’s side came in at 11th, while Miami topped the billing. This will be all too personal for the Fighting Irish, too, considering Miami played a key role in keeping them out of the playoffs in 2025. item.description: WEST LAFAYETTE, IN - SEPTEMBER 26: Notre Dame Fighting Irish players hold their helmets during the college football game between the Purdue Boilermakers and Notre Dame Fighting Irish on September 26, 2026, at Ross-Ade Stadium in West Lafayette, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Notre Dame Fighting Irish had a massive recruiting weekend for their monster matchup against the Miami Hurricanes, and it already is making a huge impact. Notre Dame gained commitments from two blue-chip players for the 2028 recruiting cycle. 4-Star EDGE Asa Burch from Ohio and 4-Star RB Zaiden Jernigan from Mississippi have both publicly committed to Notre Dame and its 2028 class. BREAKING: Top247 running back Zaiden Jernigan, one of the best in the 2028 class, has committed to Notre Dame. Why the Irish ☘️? He spoke in-depth with me about his decision to “choose hard.” VIP Story: https://t.co/MEeilpm8wl @zaiden_6 @247Sports . @irishillustratd pic.twitter.com/M5krRqOYCw — Tom Loy (@TomLoy247) November 7, 2026 BREAKING: Elite 2028 EDGE Asa Burch has Committed to Notre Dame, he tells me for @Rivals The 6’5 225 EDGE chose the Fighting Irish over Michigan and Penn State He’s ranked as a Top 40 Recruit in the 2028 Rivals300 https://t.co/MfxIxtMmLb pic.twitter.com/8DKPlBq277 — Hayes Fawcett (@Hayesfawcett3) November 7, 2026 This is a major win for the Irish in more ways than JUST the talent these two are bringing with them to South Bend. Burch is from Warren High School, which almost never sends its best talent to Notre Dame. Jernigan is from Mississippi, which again, is not a place that Notre Dame generally pulls its talent from. With this being the 2028 class, we are still over a year away from signing day — so I’ll have more on this haul in the near future.

item.title: Analysis: Turnovers, missed tackles and lack of discipline cost No. 9 BYU a chance to upset No. 3 Utah
item.description: BYU Cougars quarterback Bear Bachmeier (47) falls short of a touchdown during the first half of a football game against the Utah Utes, Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026, at Rice-Eccles Stadium in Salt Lake City. | Erin Hooley, Deseret News A lot of numbers were thrown around before No. 9 BYU traveled to No. 3 Utah in the most significant football rivalry game in the long, heated and often tumultuous series between the Beehive State foes. When it was over in front of 52,901 at Rice-Eccles Stadium, only one digit really stood out. That would be four. The upset-minded Cougars blew a rare opportunity to get a win in Salt Lake City, get their College Football Playoff hopes back on track and snap their rivals’ nation-best winning streak on Saturday afternoon. The number everybody on the blue side will remember is the four turnovers BYU committed against a ballhawking Utah defense that was otherwise pushed around most of the day. So the undefeated Utes ran off with a 28-20 victory — snapping the Cougars’ three-game winning streak against them — and put what was once the most-anticipated season in school history on life support. Although BYU head coach Kalani Sitake wouldn’t dare say it himself — preferring to heap praise upon the Utes than say the Cougars simply committed far too many turnovers and mental mistakes to win — the truth is that BYU faltered in the second half, while Utah soared. The Utes had the clutch gene in beating the Cougars for the first time since 2019, and BYU did not. The Cougars got away with an awful second half in their 28-24 win over then-No. 2 Notre Dame that now seems like a distant memory, but that kind of failure never works in this rivalry. Neither team is ever out of the games in this wild and wacky rivalry. Leave it to BYU freshman Legend Glasker to sum up what happened to the Cougars (4-2, 7-2), who must now win out and hope that either Houston or Texas Tech loses down the stretch. “I feel like the second half we got too big-headed and thought the game was ours and it just slipped away,” he said. item.title: Utah’s Big Win Proves Dampier Is Heisman-Ready
item.description: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Utah put an end to the three-game losing streak in the Holy War with a 28-20 win over BYU on Saturday. The third-ranked Utes stayed unbeaten and kept their College Football Playoff hopes alive. Devon Dampier accounted for four total touchdowns to lead the way. It was a statement game for the program, but the coach wants the team to keep grinding. Dampier Makes His Case Devon Dampier is the Big 12’s clearest Heisman candidate after Saturday’s performance. He has now thrown for a touchdown in eight of nine games this season while adding a pair of rushing scores against BYU. The senior signal-caller threw two scores and ran for two more against the Cougars. He also caught a 29-yard pass between two defenders to keep a drive alive. The Big 12 has not had a national finalist since TCU in 2022. A Heisman winner has not come from the conference since Oklahoma left. If the league is going to break that streak, it has to be Dampier. Defense Forces The Turnovers The Utes defense picked off BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier four times on Saturday. Bachmeier threw for 272 yards and a touchdown, but he could not protect the ball. Through the initial eight games of the season, he totaled four picks, plus two additional ones in the fourth quarter versus Utah. Both of those late interceptions happened inside the end zone. Utah forced three turnovers in the second half and shut out the Cougars for the rest of the game. The defense held BYU to just 39 yards in the third quarter. That stop allowed Utah to take the lead for good. Utah started the game with a burst of speed that put them ahead 14-0 in less than five minutes. It took just 75 seconds for the Utes to drive 75 yards for the first score. Utah’s opening drive leading to a touchdown marked the eighth occurrence this season. The team has now outscored opponents 103-9 in the opening quarter through nine games. Head coach Morgan Scalley knows the team is in the driver’s seat for a title, but he does not want them to get comfortable. Following the game, Scalley said on the broadcast, “This was a big win, not THE big win,” according to Fox Sports . The Utes remain 9-0 and 6-0 in the Big 12.

item.title: Why Milwaukee Bucks’ Brayden Burries isn’t satisfied with his double-double vs. Toronto Raptors
item.description: Brayden Burries was one of the bright spots in the Milwaukee Bucks ‘ 121-107 NBA Cup loss to the Toronto Raptors on Friday night. The Arizona product tallied his first double-double of the season with 21 points, 11 rebounds, and six assists on 8-for-14 shooting in 38 minutes. The 21-year-old combo guard drove and cut relentlessly to the paint, including his baseline tomahawk jam early in the second quarter, scoring 14 of his 21 points there. Day by day, it’s becoming clear why starting Burries is the right move for the Milwaukee Bucks moving forward. Brayden Burries’ hustle energizes the Milwaukee Bucks Nov 6, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Bucks guard Brayden Burries (0) reaches for a loose ball against Toronto Raptors guard Jamal Shead (1) in the first quarter at Fiserv Forum. Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images Brayden Burries earned his spot in the starting lineup not only because of his offensive potential, but also his energy. The No. 10 pick in this summer’s NBA Draft said he worked on his rebounding, which has been evident in the past few games, although he isn’t fully satisfied with his performance because they haven’t won much. “I’ve been getting a good amount of rebounds, but then in the second half I don’t get as much, so I need to get more. Or at least go. I feel like me not going; like, even if I go and I don’t get it, now I’m ready to play defense, ready to pick up. Even like Minnesota (on Nov. 2), I had nine, but I think I had like six or seven in the first half. Then last game (in Boston), I had a good amount in the first half. So, it’s that second half I gotta keep rebounding. That’s the main thing. That’s what gets me going,” Burries said. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images Milwaukee Bucks guard Tyler Herro strongly believes Brayden Burries is on his way to becoming one of the team’s best players, and he’s excited to see his growth throughout the course of his rookie campaign. “I love Brayden, that’s my rook,” Herro said postgame. “I love seeing his growth. He’s going to continue to be, obviously, one of the better players on this team but one of the better players in the league as he continues to grow. So I’m excited to just see how he grows. As we previously reported when Liao first examined the two collisions , the doctor raised the possibility that the earlier contact and subsequent injury could have been related. That connection has not been medically established. Still, the earlier tackle raises a separate question about the NFL’s rules. Should the NFL Have Fined Jack Campbell? According to the NFL’s official player-safety rules , players are prohibited from lowering their heads to initiate forcible contact with their helmets. That includes contact with an opponent’s body, not just the head or neck. The rule exists because leading with the helmet can put both the tackler and the opposing player at significant risk. Based on the available footage and Liao’s observations, I believe Campbell’s earlier tackle warranted a serious look from the league. Does that automatically mean he deserved a fine? No. The NFL must determine whether a player actually violated the rule, including whether the contact was avoidable and initiated with the helmet. But here’s what makes the situation interesting. According to the NFL’s official Week 8 accountability report , 31 plays resulted in fines, including a $23,882 penalty against Cleveland’s Tyson Campbell for illegal helmet use. Jack Campbell wasn’t among the players fined. And that brings me back to my original question. Did Campbell’s Serious Injury Change the NFL’s Thinking? Consider the circumstances. Campbell appeared to lead with his helmet on an earlier tackle. Seven plays later, he suffered a serious neck injury that required hospitalization. By the time the NFL reviewed its Week 8 discipline, Campbell’s condition had become a major concern across the football world. Would the league really want to send a fine notice to a player recovering from such a frightening injury? It’s possible that the extraordinary circumstances influenced the league’s thinking. But there is no public evidence that NFL officials intentionally overlooked the tackle or declined to fine Campbell because of his injury . There is also a perfectly reasonable alternative explanation. The league might have reviewed the play and determined that it did not meet the standard for discipline. That distinction matters. The NFL says its officiating department reviews every play from every game, with potential violations referred for additional evaluation. What we don’t know is how Campbell’s specific tackle was evaluated or why it didn’t result in a fine. And until the league provides that information, nobody can responsibly claim the decision was motivated by sympathy. Player Safety Should Come Before Everything Else Look, I’m a Lions fan. I want nothing more than to see Jack Campbell make a full recovery and eventually return to doing what he loves. The last thing I’m worried about is whether he saves a few thousand dollars. But the NFL has spent years emphasizing player safety and eliminating dangerous tackling techniques. Those standards should remain consistent, regardless of the outcome of a particular play. If Campbell’s earlier tackle violated the rule, his subsequent injury shouldn’t automatically erase that violation. And if the tackle was legal, the NFL made the correct decision not to fine him. As we reported following Saturday’s roster announcement , Detroit has officially placed Campbell on injured reserve as he continues his recovery. His health is infinitely more important than any potential financial penalty. But there is a bigger issue worth discussing. The NFL understandably wants players to change dangerous tackling habits before someone suffers a serious injury. If the earlier play was an example of the technique the league wants eliminated, it deserves scrutiny regardless of what happened afterward. So, did Jack Campbell’s injury influence the NFL’s decision not to fine him? We don’t know. But considering the circumstances, I believe it’s a question worth asking. And one the NFL could answer by explaining how it evaluated the play.

item.title: Cesc Fabregas emerges as Man United’s top managerial target as INEOS get in touch with intermediaries
item.description: Cesc Fabregas emerges as Man United’s top managerial target as INEOS get in touch with intermediaries Sunday’s Premier League clash against Aston Villa will be pivotal for Michael Carrick if he is to remain in charge of Manchester United beyond the November international break. INEOS had given him three games to steady the ship, but it fell apart in the second half against Chelsea after a promising first 45 minutes. Thankfully, the players responded with a brilliant come-from-behind win against AS Roma, easing the pressure on the head coach . However, the co-owners continue to consider making a change in the dugout, with multiple names in contention. Cesc Fabregas now a top target Director of football Jason Wilcox prefers Eddie Howe and contact has been made , while recruitment chief Christopher Vivell wants Julian Nagelsmann. The German is reportedly not too keen , and the former Newcastle United boss is not considered the most attractive option. Some within the hierarchy would prefer a more ambitious name , but Unai Emery appears set to remain at Villa Park for the foreseeable future. Cesc Fabregas, whose Como team dismantled the Red Devils, is also in the running and, according to TEAMtalk , United have discussed his name at length. INEOS have started talks In fact, the 20-time English league champions have even contacted intermediaries to gauge the Spaniard’s interest in a potential move in the future. “Sources can reveal that Fabregas has once again featured prominently in conversations. “TEAMtalk understands Fabregas’s name has been discussed at length at United and that intermediaries have been spoken to in order to gauge the former Arsenal and Chelsea midfielder’s current situation.” This uncertainty is exactly why Carrick has been given a longer rope. He needs to make his second chance count, and the club’s underperforming stars must deliver. Antonio Conte is another ambitious name on the club’s radar, but the Italian’s transfer demands are considered significant. Hence, the reluctance. Feature image Marco Luzzani via Getty Images online polls

item.description: Credit: Melina Myers-Imagn Images Patriots makes receiver roster move amid AJ Brown’s injury absence appeared first on ClutchPoints . Coach Mike Vrabel’s New England Patriots are 5-3 on the season heading into Week 9’s home game against the Green Bay Packers, and QB Drake Maye is running out of weapons . Maye has a tough task on his hands against Jordan Love and the Packers with star wideout AJ Brown ’s injury concerns continuing. The Pats made a move to replenish their receiver room with a familiar face, according to Adam Schefter of ESPN, who shared the news that Mack Hollins was added to the team’s 53-man roster from the practice squad. Hollins has played in four games with the Pats this season, and has caught 15 passes for 209 yards with a long of 26. At 6-foot-4, the 33-year-old North Carolina Tar Heels alumnus provides a similarly big target to Brown that Maye can push the ball downfield when the situation warrants it. Hollins’ best receiving yards season came in 2025, when he recorded 550 yards with Vrabel and Maye’s team en route to a Super Bowl appearance. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The Patriots will be without potential star running back TreVeyon Henderson against Green Bay, as Henderson got a message from his head coach . Rhamondre Stevenson will start at running back, giving Maye a versatile target out of the backfield who has caught 20 passes for over 200 yards and a touchdown this season. The Patriots aren’t at full strength, but they’re still going strong at 5-3 heading into Week 3. Hollins is just the kind of veteran leader they need with Brown on the shelf as they move forward. item.title: Thunder’s Ajay Mitchell reveals aggressive approach after scoring a career-high
item.description: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Thunder’s Ajay Mitchell reveals aggressive approach after scoring a career-high appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . For the second time this season, Oklahoma City Thunder’s Ajay Mitchell set a new career high with 35 points in a 128-97 win over the Memphis Grizzlies. While Mitchell has often been the second-leading scorer since the Thunder lost three starters due to long-term injures, All-Star Shai Gilgeous-Alexander finished with 28 points on 11-for-22 shooting. Mitchell addressed his approach during his postgame media availability. “I was just trying to be aggressive out there; see what the defense would give us, and just try to play the game,” Mitchell said. “Every night is going to be different. So, I just go into every game with the same mindset, going out there and playing, and not worrying about anything else.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Thunder’s Ajay Mitchell went 14-for-20 from the floor, including 4-of-7 from deep, and finished with five assists, and one rebound. Oklahoma City is 4-2 since losing Jalen Williams, Cason Wallace, and All-Star Chet Holmgren to their respective injuries. Williams and Wallace will be re-evaluated before the end of the regular season, and Holmgren is expected to miss 8-to-10 weeks with a right knee injury. For Mitchell, staying focus to every detail is vital for the shot-handed Thunder’s success this season. “Staying confident no matter what’s going on,” Mitchell said. “I know the amount of work I put in. So, when I go out there and it’s not falling, I’m not worried. I’m really focused on just helping this team win. Every possession matters. So, for me, it’s trying to move on really quick to the next one. No matter if shots are going or not. That’s really been my mindset these past two years. I try to keep it like that.” Mitchell is averaging 26.0 points on 56.6/38.5/76.5 shooting splits, 4.3 rebounds, and 3.3 assists across his last three games. Thunder head coach Mark Daigneault commended his team for stringing together wins without most of its core players. “I thought we got our feet underneath us,” Daigneault said. “And gained some confidence. It was obviously a tough week. We have kind of a new collection of guys. We have to learn each other. I have to learn that, and that took a little bit of calibration, but the guys are doing a great job.” The Thunder will host the Washington Wizards on the second night of a back-to-back on Saturday. In Ball State 's second game of the season, High Point rolled into Worthen Arena and landed a haymaker. The Cardinals fell behind early and never managed to take the lead, falling to the Panthers, 78-71, at home on Saturday, Nov. 7. "One of those shoot-yourself-in-the-foot games," Sallee said. "I feel like every time we got it to within striking distance, we just shot ourselves in the foot a little bit. Credit High Point, that's a good basketball team, well-coached, a lot of passion, and they're clearly going to win a lot of basketball games. These early season tests, we could go play a bunch of different kinds of people, and maybe it'd be fool's gold. "But man, you get punched in the mouth, and that's when you learn the most about yourself." "I'd say it's probably a mental thing and kind of just a toughness thing too, to go put it on the rim and also have that mentality to also score it as well," Towers said. "We had good looks, we just couldn't finish them." Despite the offensive inefficiencies, Ball State was able to keep things close in the second half thanks to some defensive adjustments that kept High Point from lighting them up from 3-point land again. The Cardinals' perimeter defense was much more aggressive and limited the Panthers' outside looks. High Point went 3-for-9 from deep in the second half and had multiple scoreless droughts of two-plus minutes, but Ball State just couldn't string together a long run of its own. Meanwhile, fifth-year guard Taylor Feldman got the hot hand for High Point, scoring 12 second-half points to finish with a team-high 21. "We did talk about the fact that we knew they were going to shoot it, and we let them make seven of them," Sallee said. "We were just soft. We were so bad preparing that I just think it took us about 25 minutes to figure it out." Towers led Ball State with a 23-point, 11-rebound double-double, while freshman Lillian Barnes continued her strong start to her collegiate career with 20 points, seven rebounds and three assists off the bench. Third-year guard Grace Kingery overcame a slow first half to finish with 13 points but shot an uncharacteristic 1-for-8 from distance. Sallee took issue with his team's lack of preparedness for the matchup and called them out multiple times in the postgame press conference for what he perceived as bad practices in the lead up to the game. "We were putrid in practice yesterday," Sallee said. "There's some teams that have the maturity level to be really bad in practice, I've had a couple of those, believe me — the Ally Becki group was not great in practice every day — but when it came to game time, they knew the scout, they knew the job, and they went out and executed. Our team showed me that we can't, so we can't practice like we did on Friday and expect to play any different." Ball State's upcoming schedule doesn't get any easier, as the Cardinals are preparing to host back-to-back top-25 teams. No. 7 Louisville comes to town on Thursday, Nov. 12, and No. 22 Illinois will follow on Wednesday, Nov. 18. As Ball State looks to regroup and potentially pull off an upset or two, the players have heard Sallee's message and plan to approach future practices with a new energy. "As a goal for our team, leading up to practices or whatever, I think we all need to bring more energy," Towers said. "Focus on each other in that way, really just come together. We all know we need to practice hard and play hard, we talked about that, and we know what we have to do. It's just a matter of fact that we have to get it done." item.title: There are very few reasons for Unai Emery to leave Aston Villa for Manchester United | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Spaniard may feel some of Old Trafford’s allure when he goes there on Sunday but he is right in wanting to stay at the club with brighter prospects On Sunday afternoon, shortly before 4.30, Unai Emery will leave the tunnel at Old Trafford and walk along the touchline towards the bench. Will he glance around the grand old stadium – faded and leaking though it may be in parts – and think that he could have a part in restoring the club to former glories? Will he look at the home bench and imagine himself sitting there – or perhaps more plausibly, scuttling up and down in front of it – as the first Manchester United manager since Sir Alex Ferguson to land a league title? Perhaps not. Emery is, after all, in “advanced talks” to extend a contract at Villa that already runs to 2029. However frustrating he may find the habitual summer churn, he is good at managing it. He feels the right fit for Villa, and that is arguably the most important factor in determining success. Yet all elite managers share a robust self-belief and there is a paradoxical sense that the worse the situation gets at United, the more appealing the job becomes. Continue reading...

item.title: Martin Ødegaard extends Arsenal lead at top with winner to break Hull resistance
item.description: As most Arsenal supporters would testify, patience is a virtue. They needed plenty during the 22-year wait to be crowned Premier League champions and Mikel Arteta’s side certainly had to retain their composure as they tried to break down a dogged Hull side. They had not beaten Arsenal in 14 attempts since winning on their first visit to this ground in 2008. But with 20 minutes to play, there was still every chance that Sergej Jakirovic’s team could have pulled off one of the shocks of the season. Arsenal had already been denied a penalty just before half-time for a shirt pull on Kai Havertz in the box a week after escaping the same crime against Liverpool at Anfield, in a moment of controversy that could have been the major talking point from this match. Martin Ødegaard had other ideas and the Arsenal captain’s fifth goal of the season was enough to ensure they will go into the international break with a healthy lead over Manchester City. Enzo Maresca’s side are up next here in the league after the international break, with Arsenal having matched their record tally of 27 points from their opening 10 games. The signs look ominous for the rest, even if they were made to work for the points throughout by their opponents. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘A footballing alien’: Mamadou Sangaré soars to Premier League heights
item.description: Brentford’s Mali midfielder stood out when he was six and has shone in the Premier League since £39m transfer “When I first saw him, I thought to myself: ‘Who on earth is this player?’ laughs Youness Bengelloun as he remembers Mamadou Sangaré. With the transfer window in full swing in July 2025, the former Manchester City scout and agent was not expecting to come face to face with a “footballing alien”, but that proved the case during a visit to Rapid Vienna’s training ground. A few weeks later, Sangaré moved to Lens for around €5m. “He was impressive and what struck me was his technique and his work rate,” Bengelloun says. That’s more or less the impression Sangaré has made at every club he’s played for, including Brentford, for whom the Mali midfielder signed, from Lens, for a club-record £39m at the start of August. The 24-year-old excelled in his debut against Tottenham a few weeks later , dominating the centre of the pitch and providing the assist for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal, and has featured in every game this season, with Brighton up next. “I gave him his debut for Mali in September 2024, against Mozambique. He made an immediate impact,” says Sangaré’s former international manager Tom Saintfiet. “He’s every manager’s dream player.” Continue reading...

item.title: Rise of the ‘schooligans’: how a wave of antisocial behaviour threatens non-league football
item.description: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. The incident ended there and no one was hurt, though a police investigation has been launched. item.content:encoded: Teenage ultras are increasingly causing disorder and communities fear it will not be long before it becomes something more dangerous It is five past three on Saturday afternoon and the teenage ultras of Hednesford Town are running late. They have arrived in Chester for their team’s National League North fixture and have hailed taxis, determined to make their presence felt at the ground. But word appears to have got out about their arrival. As one car turns away from the city’s charming half-timbered houses and into narrow residential streets, half a dozen local youths appear, haring round the corner in balaclavas. They try to attack the cab and chase after it as it pulls away. The smell of pyro is everywhere. As the taxi finally gets clear, the Chester gang stops in the middle of the road, shouting and gesticulating. One lad, no older than 16, pulls a long blade from inside his trousers and brandishes it. item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! For the FA Cup, the early rounds are the juice. The first round proper to be played out over the long weekend is looking, well, proper. And on Saturday at 3pm GMT, a proper time, 31 ties will kick off. No VAR, either. At the stage when the bottom two Football League divisions join the competition, focus remains on those non-league clubs fighting for the honour of the pyramid … John Aloisi winning or choking​ the Chinese Super League , a league so ‘super’ that nine of all 16 clubs in it started the season on negative points due to ‘match-fixing, gambling and corruption’ by the way, and the league leaders not even scoring a single goal in seven hours, is really not something to lay upon someone with a bad hangover. Apropos of nothing, if anyone has any objections to my views on the Chinese Super League, please address any correspondence to: Mr K Mbappé, Madrid (there’s no point two of us getting into trouble)” – Noble Francis. As a man of a certain age frequently being reminded of how out of date I am, the recent readers’ letters regarding technical solutions to shirt-pulling (Football Daily letters passim) concerns triggered distant memories. In late 1991 I was working in the Patents Advice Centre, Newcastle Central Library. A gentleman asked for help to possibly patent an ‘invention’: a football shirt with the seams held together by Velcro, so that any tug would ‘open’ the seam and provide clear evidence to the referee of illegal cloth gathering. As I helped him search for possible equivalent innovations in our paper database (yes kids!) we chatted amiably until I asked how he had come to this seemingly simple yet brilliant innovation. He paused, reddened and began to exhale with elevated pressure: ‘Did you see Arsenal the other night? Tony Adams? Disgraceful. It should never be allowed! In fact, with this shirt it won’t be, and Arsenal will have to learn to defend decently!’ Happy memories, obviously irrelavant to the modern game” – Garren Mulloy. Not fair! Bias! (Picture me, arms wide out, mouth open, eyebrows as high as they’ll go, appealing for reason.) I wrote about skin-tight shirts the other day and you ignored it, publishing a Velcro alternative. Now you’ve published another letter about skin-tight shirts ( yesterday’s letters ), days later. And it gets letter o’ the day! What’s the literary equivalent of kicking the keeper’s water bottle in frustration? I’ve just done that” – Ken Muir. I see that Celtic finally moved up the Bigger Vase charts on Thursday night and started playing a tune when their subs Osmand, Durán and Donovan came on. Too corny but my wife actually laughed at this” – Hugh Jamieson. That was a topsy-turvy Durán Durán show at Celtic, but what else would you expect from a bunch of Wild Bhoys?” – Peter Oh. item.title: ‘In moments of pain, football comes together’: Spain says goodbye to Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but the streets of Navahermosa were fuller yet quieter to mourn the Tenerife striker at his funeral The narrow streets of Navahermosa in La Mancha were fuller than they have ever been on Thursday afternoon and quieter too. Silence accompanied the funeral cortege as its made way from the funeral home to the parish church of San Miguel Arcángel carrying Jesús de Miguel Alameda, “Demi”, the Tenerife striker who died after an on-field collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono three days earlier. Only 3,587 people live in his family’s village but now they were joined by the game he loved. “We wanted to be close to his parents, his wife and daughter. In moments of pain, football comes together more than ever,” said Luis de la Fuente. The Spain manager did not say much else; there was not much else he could say, not much anyone could. These have been dark, desperate days, days when it was impossible to assimilate what has happened, and there will be more. “We will get through this together but we will need help, professional help,” the Tenerife president, Felipe Miñambres, said. item.title: Cristiano Ronaldo merely the latest example of a great player who couldn’t let go | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There is no doubt his international career was an incredible one, but it would have been greater still if he had not lingered on the stage so long Nothing, perhaps, is quite so difficult for an elite sportsperson as timing their exit. It’s not easy for any person in any job to weigh the hope of having more to give with the desire not to linger beyond their usefulness, but it’s perhaps particularly hard for top athletes because unrealistic self-confidence is so essential to their success. It takes an almost unhealthy level of self-belief for anybody to make the sacrifices to get to the top, to dedicate themselves to such a precarious vocation, to overcome all the setbacks and injuries and failures. How can someone – whose whole life has been spent assuring themselves there are no odds they cannot overcome – accept that is it, that the time has come to say goodbye? The news that Cristiano Ronaldo has retired from international football brings with it, inevitably, a sadness. Sadness we will no longer see him skipping past a defender, or burying a neck-thrusting header, and sadness in that the end of the career of any great is a reminder of mortality; all things in time must pass. But there is also a sadness he timed his departure so badly. For at least three tournaments, there has been a sense of Ronaldo holding Portugal back. Continue reading...

item.title: Uefa faces political flashpoint over Sevastopol’s ascent in Russian football
item.description: Promotion to third tier for Crimean club would be clear violation of governing body’s rules amid conflict in Ukraine Uefa and Fifa face a decisive test of their appetite to punish Russia’s integration of teams from illegally occupied Ukrainian territory after FC Sevastopol, from Crimea, won promotion to the country’s professional third tier. Sevastopol were declared champions of group one in Football National League (FNL) 2B, in effect Russia’s fourth division, last month and are believed to have applied for a licence to compete at the level above. Should it be granted and they proceed to FNL 2A, it would appear a violation of Uefa rules that prohibit Crimean clubs from playing in competitions organised by the Russian Football Union (RFU). The governing body would come under severe pressure to extend sanctions on European football’s pariah state, whose club and national teams are banned from competing in international tournaments. item.title: Harry Kane’s Ballon d’Or party gives way to anxiety-filled hangover for Bayern Munich | Andy Brassell
item.description: Dortmund did not read the script, remaining level on points with the defending champions at the top of the table It was the moment they had all been … not so much waiting for, but planning, pushing and yearning for. In the videos that announce the starting lineup on the giant scoreboard before kick-off, every Bayern Munich player turns to face the camera with their personal salute, greeting or goal celebration, the playful progression from the standard folding of arms. Except on Saturday evening, the No 9 turned around smiling, and cradling the golden trophy. In the midweek DFB Pokal stroll against Magdeburg there had been a salute, the players welcoming Harry Kane on to the pitch with a guard of honour to commemorate his Ballon d’Or victory two nights before. This, however, was the real party, the moment where the England captain’s and Bayern’s successful union and the apex it has reached was celebrated in front of a global audience. There was every reason to believe it would be a full and satisfying victory lap, even in Der Klassiker, with proper competition so often bringing the best out of the Rekordmeister. Before this weekend, the last time Folarin Balogun scored was in the United States’ 2-0 win over Bosnia and Herzegovina at this past summer’s World Cup. In the immediate aftermath, the outlook for Balogun seemed rosy; an ascendant player who could muster a goal in tense games. At half-time against Bosnia, US fans weren’t just wondering how far his team could advance – they were sizing Balogun up against some of the world’s best strikers. But for most of the ensuing four months, Balogun has been in limbo. His breakout World Cup was overshadowed by a red card in that same game against Bosnia and Herzegovina, followed by a scandal of which he wanted no part. Just as it seemed a summer move away from Monaco could get his club career on track, he broke off a possible deadline-day move to Everton after a lengthy visit to the training grounds and a medical he felt was improperly handled. item.title: Rampant Salford hint that Beckham’s lofty ambitions are not a pipe dream
item.description: The aim of reaching the Championship looks more realistic for a Manchester club in the shadow of City and United After seven seasons in League Two, Salford City are finally threatening to match the hype brought by their high-profile owners. First it was the Class of ’92 who guided them up through the non-league system into the fourth tier but failed to progress any further. Gary Neville and David Beckham remain, part of a new group that took over in May 2025, with this year beginning to look transformational after securing an eighth straight win, against Exeter, to put them five points clear at the top. The budget has increased, allowing the club to sign a number of players who will feel they are above League Two standard. Striker Macaulay Langstaff arrived from Millwall; the last time he played at this level, he scored 28 league goals in a season for Notts County. Match-winner Will Aimson spent the past two seasons in the division above with Wigan and has dropped down because of Salford’s project. Continue reading...

item.title: Mourinho’s plan comes together as Real Madrid relaunch with clásico statement | Sid Lowe
item.description: It was just like old times as José Mourinho ended a night at Camp Nou with a knee slide and three points José Mourinho had already done the por qu é? , the printout and the press conference no-show in under 100 days. Now he’s done a knee slide too, and in the perfect place: back where it all began and where it can all begin again. When Kylian Mbappé scored the first in the clásico on Sunday night, Real Madrid’s manager hardly moved, sitting in the shadow of the bench – but when the striker got the second to win it with time running out, that was different. Mourinho leapt into the light, throwing himself to the grass, the knees of a 63-year-old’s trousers muddy as a schoolboy’s, stuck his tongue out and pumped his fists. He does so love it when a plan comes together. To the right of him, the bench was emptying, subs joining the players in sprinting towards the south-west corner. As they leapt about, dodging the bottles thrown towards them from the end, way, way up in the furthest corner and stuck inside a glass box like a bunch of David Blaines, the small group of Madrid fans who had come were going mad. In the main stand, a thousand phones were raised. And 600 kilometres west, back in Boadilla, Thibaut Courtois was watching his teammates from the sofa at home, presumably wrapped in a blanket and cradling a cup of Lemsip. On the morning of the biggest game there is, he awoke with flu, forced to miss out. Continue reading...

item.title: The horse that ushered in Manchester United’s tragic arc | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: There’s plenty of blame to go around at Old Trafford. Like all downfalls it started with a seemingly small, unconnected moment Sign up for our free newsletter here And so here we are again, at that point as the nights draw in and Manchester United prepare to sack a manager . Autumn: season of mists, mellow fruitfulness and a crisis at Old Trafford. Sunday’s 3-0 home defeat to Bournemouth , coming on the back of last week’s 4-1 reverse against Como, made clear what many had feared from the moment Michael Carrick was given the job on a permanent basis: that he isn’t up to it. But then, who could be? When you’ve burned through a long list of managers in 13 years, it’s perhaps worth considering whether the manager is really the problem. Could some blame perhaps go to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, or the chief executive, Omar Berrada, the people making the appointments? Or perhaps to Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the cost-cutting tax exile and minority shareholder with responsibility for sporting operations? Or to the Glazer family, who plunged the club into debt with a leveraged buyout in 2005 and have since made calamitous decision after calamitous decision, reducing the most successful club in English league history to a mid-table laughing stock with a roof that leaks symbolically ? This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Continue reading...

Finally, a “W” followed by a jab to the heart. “Dead. Man. Walking,” he declared, pausing for effect between words and briefly falling into an Oscar-worthy zombie stupor. “That’s how it feels.” To an offbeat press conference genre containing seagulls following trawlers and self-proclaimed special ones, it was a crazy new entry worthy of its subsequent viral nature. item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game.
